evals.name: add-cost-profile
evals.prompt: I run OpenMCP with targets forge-primary, sentinel-primary, and sage-primary plus a balanced profile. Add a cost profile that runs implement on a new Codex target using gpt-5-mini while review stays on sentinel-primary and consult stays on sage-primary. Write the exact global TOML additions.
evals.expected_output: TOML adds one global Codex target with model gpt-5-mini and a [profiles.cost] table mapping implement directly to the new target, review to sentinel-primary, and consult to sage-primary. It uses backend_profile rather than target profile when needed, adds no intermediate grouping section, includes no secrets, and calls reload for validation without claiming a restart is required.

evals.name: project-override-reviewer
evals.prompt: For project /home/me/app only, send review to a stricter Pi reviewer using gpt-5.6-sol with high reasoning, isolation, and read-only mode. Keep implement and consult inherited from the global quality profile. Which files should change?
evals.expected_output: Adds the reviewer target globally in ~/.openmcp/config.toml. Adds only [profiles.quality] review = strict-target-id to /home/me/app/.openmcp/config.toml, with no project target definition. Calls reload to validate the global target and explains that the project profile override reloads when used.
